newsitem.title: USA: Quake hits southern California, no damage reported.
newsitem.headline: Quake hits southern California, no damage reported.

text.p: A moderate earthquake shook the San Diego area late on Friday, rocking mobile homes and rattling windows, but no serious damages were reported, authorities said.

The temblor, measuring 4.9 on the Richter scale, struck at 8:14 p.m. PDT (0314 GMT Saturday) in northeastern San Diego County, a spokesman for the California Institute of Technology said. It was felt 50 miles (80 km) away in downtown San Diego.
The epicentre of the quake was close to the small town of Borrego Springs in the foothills of the Santa Rosa Mountains, the spokesman said.

A spokeswoman for the San Diego County Sheriff's Dept. said their phone lines were jammed for an hour after the earthquake by anxious callers. Residents reported that their mobile homes were rocked by the quake and others reported rattling windows, but there were no reports of serious damage.
"I imagine a few ornaments might have fallen, but that's about the extent of it," the spokeswoman said.
